newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weak, gas oil flat.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weak, gas oil flat.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker on Monday, traders said.
Naphtha ended $3 lower and high freight rates and quiet end-user demand continued to limit trading.
A Spanish end-user was rumoured to have sold a Skikda cargo for Feb 5-9 loading, to be stemmed together with another cargo and shipped to the States, one source said.
The deal could not be confirmed.
Gasoline eased slightly but demand from Lebanon and other eastern Med destinations was supportive. The arb to the U.S. appeared shut but recent U.S. buying has tightened local supply.
Gas oil trade was slow on Monday as the market digested recent volatility. "People don't want to do much when it's uncertain," said one trader.
An Italian 20kt heating oil cargo was sold at fob high +$3 for delivery in early February.
Traders said high shipping costs in the Med have made it difficult to move material out of the region.
"Even though we are long, and there's some international demand, the lack of ships and high cost is limiting trade," said one trader.
High and low sulphur fuel oil was weaker in line with NWE.
A Syrian tender was announced to sell two 50,000 tonne cargoes of fuel oil in February. The tender closes on Tuesday.
Med fuel oil swaps slipped to as low as $90 fob Med, around three dollars down from last week.
Russian fuel oil exports from the Black Sea were assessed at around 200-250,000 tonnes in January, compared to almost twice that figure in December.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weak, with offers expected to be around $116 cif Med. Activity was muted.
